objective.statement: Match each note value with the rest of the same length.
successCriteria: I know a rest is a silence with a symbol for each note length.
I can match each note value to its rest.
I can count rests and notes together.

explanation.text: Music is made of silence as well as sound. A rest is a sign for silence, and every note value has a rest that lasts exactly as long.

music.textAlternative: A semibreve followed by a semibreve rest, then a minim followed by a minim rest.

explanation.caption: The semibreve rest hangs below a line; the minim rest sits on top of it.

explanation.text: The semibreve rest is a small block hanging from the 4th line. The minim rest is the same block sitting on top of the 3rd line. Both last as long as their notes.

music.textAlternative: A crotchet, a quaver and a semiquaver, each followed by the rest of the same length.

explanation.caption: Crotchet, quaver and semiquaver rests. Each lasts as long as the note beside it.

explanation.text: Two rests, two beats of silence. Count the beats of rests in exactly the same way as notes: just say nothing!

music.textAlternative: Two bars. The first has a crotchet, a crotchet rest and a minim. The second has two quavers, a crotchet rest and a crotchet.

steps: Press Play all and tap the beat. Notice that the rest takes up a beat of silence.
Count the first bar: 'one, (rest), three-four'. The rest is one beat.
In the second bar, the two quavers fill beat one, then the rest is beat two.
demonstration.textAlternative: Two bars of rhythm with a one-beat rest in each. Playing them shows that the silence lasts exactly as long as a note.

guided.prompt: Which rest lasts as long as a semiquaver?
hints: Semibreve rests hang below a line; minim rests sit on top of one.
Every note value has a rest of the same length and the same name.

feedback.correct: Every note has a rest of the same name.

mistakes.halved-or-doubled: That value is twice (or half) as long. Count it in crotchet beats and compare.
mistakes.dot-misread: Remember: a dot adds half of the note's own value. Work out that half, then add it.
mistakes.note-rest-confusion: Check the shape carefully. A rest that hangs below its line lasts longer than one that sits on top of it.
mistakes.tie-dot-confusion: A tie joins two notes into one sound, so add both values together.
mistakes.tuplet-ignored: Those notes are a tuplet, so they share a different amount of time. Look at the number written over them.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. Try counting each value in crotchet beats.

guided.prompt: How many crotchet beats do these notes and rests last altogether?

2.reason: A rest lasts as long as the note of the same name, so rests count towards the total too.

3.reason: Count again, one note at a time, in crotchet beats.

12.reason: Count again, one note at a time, in crotchet beats.

Add the beats one note or rest at a time.
